issues.description: The template's Farm.java does not declare the expected animals aggregation field (a List<Animal> named animals) required by the problem statement UML and shown in the solution. The exercise expects Farm to hold a List<Animal> (initialized in the no-arg constructor) with corresponding getter/setter and addAnimal(Animal) method; the template file lacks this attribute and related API, which will prevent students from implementing or testing the required functionality as specified.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template Farm.java to declare a private List<Animal> animals field, initialize it to a new ArrayList<>() in a no-argument constructor, and provide the getter/setter and addAnimal(Animal) method signatures as described in the problem statement. This will align the template with the UML and the solution implementation and allow students to implement the remaining behaviors.

issues.description: The template Farm.java contains structural/syntactic problems: the class is named AnimalFarm instead of Farm and the file includes an extra package declaration and duplicated class content nested inside a method, making the file uncompilable and inconsistent with the problem statement and solution. Students will be confused by the incorrect class name and by the invalid Java code, preventing a straightforward implementation of the required Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a clean Farm.java stub: ensure a single package declaration at the top, declare public class Farm { ... }, and remove any duplicate/embedded package or class declarations. The class name must be Farm to match the problem statement and solution. Include method stubs (addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong) and the animals attribute as described so students have a compilable starting point.

issues.description: The template provides a class named AnimalFarm (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) while the problem statement and the solution expect a class named Farm. This mismatch between 'AnimalFarm' and 'Farm' is likely to confuse students: assignment text and tests refer to Farm, but the starter code declares a differently named class, preventing a clear mapping from requirement to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from AnimalFarm to Farm (and ensure the file content and constructor match the expected Farm API). This will align the template with the problem statement and the solution, removing the naming mismatch students would otherwise encounter.
